title: Magentic-One: A Generalist Multi-Agent System for Solving Complex Tasks

model.params_source: assumed (the paper names the model - 'the default multimodal LLM we use for all agents (except the ComputerTerminal) is gpt-4o-2024-05-13' - but reports no decoding parameters; the released AutoGen code would decide them)

task.subset_rule: the authors' own WebArena test split: MD5 of each task's template id, the 422 tasks whose hash starts with a digit 0-7 go to validation, the remaining 390 to test (Sec. 5.1). The split is reproducible from the rule; the paper reports 30.5% (119 of 390) on it.
task.approximation: BLOCKED, not runnable by this harness. A WebArena task is a multi-step episode inside five self-hosted websites (shopping, shopping admin, Postmill forum, GitLab, maps plus a Wikipedia mirror) that must be deployed from the benchmark's Docker images and reset between tasks; Magentic-One is a multi-agent loop (Orchestrator, WebSurfer, FileSurfer, Coder, ComputerTerminal) that issues many model calls per step, and success is decided by the benchmark's per-task evaluation scripts run against the live site state. The runner sends one stateless chat completion per item and hooks may not call an API.

items.source: WebArena (Zhou et al. 2024), https://github.com/web-arena-x/webarena - 812 tasks plus the site images and per-task evaluators; Magentic-One is released at https://aka.ms/magentic-one (AutoGen 0.4)
items.config_or_split: the 390 test tasks of the authors' MD5 split

fields.label: the task's evaluation script (string match, URL match or program-checked site state)

items.license: WebArena: Apache-2.0; Magentic-One / AutoGen: MIT (CC-BY-4.0 for the paper)
items.access_note: Not fetched: the benchmark is a set of Docker site images plus evaluation scripts, not a table of items, and its images are far over the 50 MB download limit for this batch. Both repositories are public and named in the paper.

prompt.user_template:
{task_intent}

[This website is] a Postmill forum populated with a large sample of data crawled from Reddit. Postmill is similar to Reddit, but the UI is distinct, and 'subreddits' begin with /f/ rather than /r/

placeholders.task_intent: the WebArena task, e.g. 'Tell me the count of comments that have received more downvotes than upvotes for the user who made the latest post on the Showerthoughts forum.'

prompt.source_location: Sec. 5.1 'Implementation Details' (the Postmill clarification text, quoted verbatim) and the example task quoted in the same section
prompt.verbatim: partial: only the Postmill clarification is printed, and the paper says 'We include similar prompts for the three other WebArena sites' without printing them. The per-agent system prompts, the Orchestrator's ledger prompts and the benchmark-specific final-answer prompt are in the released code, not in the paper. The typographic quotes around the quoted passage are the paper's; the opening bracket of '[This website is]' is the authors' own insertion.

output.postprocess: the orchestrator's final answer is compared by the task's own evaluator; intermediate steps change the state of the website

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: Task completion rate: share of tasks whose WebArena evaluator passes (exact or fuzzy answer match plus the required end state of the site).
metric.judge: none (program-checked; some WebArena evaluators use a model-based fuzzy match)
metric.original_location: Sec. 5.2: '35.1% of tasks (148 of 422), falling to 30.5% (119 of 390) for the test set'; Table 1 reports 32.8% over all 812 tasks

cost.cost_note: Order of magnitude only: 390 tasks x tens of agent steps, each step a multimodal call carrying a screenshot and the accessibility tree. The paper gives no token or cost figure for WebArena.

open_points: harness: WebArena has to be deployed (five site containers plus a Wikipedia mirror, reset between tasks) and Magentic-One has to be run against it from the released AutoGen code with our own key. That is a separate arm, not something this runner can express; a human must decide whether it is in scope.
prompts: only one of the four site clarification prompts is printed, and none of the agent prompts are, so the input would come from the repository rather than the paper.

the o1-preview configuration of Magentic-One is not reproducible at all (dead preview model), which is why only the GPT-4o WebArena cell was triaged; GAIA and AssistantBench results in Table 1 use the GPT-4o + o1-preview combination.
notes: The test split is well defined (MD5 of the template id) and the paper is unusually careful about it, so the comparison target itself is clean - the obstacle is purely that the benchmark is a live environment plus a multi-agent loop. Table 1's 32.8% is over all 812 tasks; the 30.5% cell used here is the held-out split the authors say they evaluated only once.
